section_I_attitude_6th_term_entry.insertion_point: gm-pentad-operationalization-manual.md, after A.5 PURPOSE, as new subsection A.6 ATTITUDE (6th term)

entry.operational_definition: Attitude = the sixth dramatistic term (added by Burke himself, GM-09 1962 Addendum; operationalized in Rhetoric of Motives). Names an INCIPIENT ACT: a disposition/leaning/orientation toward action not yet (or not necessarily) overt; the suspended/symbolic-rehearsal mode mediating dynamis and energeia; carries affective/evaluative tone.
entry.question_answered: in what disposition / with what orientation? (transverse — askable of any of the five placement-terms)
paradigm_examples: 'attitude being an incipient act' — poetic/scientific/rhetorical triad (RM-01 p.42)
avarice as 'property' translated into an agent's attitude (RM-01 p.24)
acting-together's shared 'attitudes' make men consubstantial (RM-01 p.21)
persuasion-to-attitude vs persuasion-to-action; attitude as leaning/inclination (RM-02 pp.50-51)
'renunciation and advance fused in one attitude' (RM-06 p.251)
standoffishness of pure persuasion as attitudinal stance (RM-07 pp.269-271)
(Grammar seeds) attitude as beginning of acts (GM-06 p.236); incipient action (GM-06 p.235); Urn-as-Attitude (GM-10 p.458)
decision_rules: disposition not yet issued in completed external conduct -> Attitude (else Act)
disposition deliberately/constitutively HELD without consummation -> Attitude (suspended-act sense)
supplies disposition-with-which rather than end-toward-which -> Attitude, not Purpose
carries affective/evaluative tone coloring an act -> Attitude as tonal modifier
rhetoric/poetic aims at orientation only, no overt act -> persuasion-to-attitude (more general target)
entry.status_modifier_not_box: Attitude is TRANSVERSE — a dispositional modifier (disposition-with-which) askable of Act/Scene/Agent/Agency/Purpose; best represented as a COLUMN across all five (as in Grammar Section E), not a sixth ratio-row.

calleja_pim_mapping.rationale: Affective is the response-state dimension; already carries Layer-B target 'ATTITUDE (Burke's later sixth term)' (ig-pim A.5/E.1); player-attitude register maps here (rm-attitude-as-sixth-term E).

ontological_target.target: Aristotelian pathē (Rhetoric II) + hexis/dunamis (attitude as dunamis-as-hexis); cross-anchor Gross 2017
ontological_target.note: this is the ONE pentad term Burke himself supplements (GM-09 Addendum) — entry is burke-direct in architecture even where grounding is anticipatory

entry.ratio_note: Attitude does NOT enter the 10-ratio matrix as an 11th pair; it MODIFIES each existing ratio (an act-purpose ratio can be eager/reluctant/ironic). Attitude-ratios = modulations, not new pairs.

section_III_consubstantiation_status.III_2_replace_blocker_with_consolidation: Bridge consolidated. RM-01 supplies the burke-direct ground the Grammar only seeded (GM-00 p.xix; GM-02 type-16; GM-13 peripety): consubstantiation defined at p.21 ('substantially one' yet 'individual locus of motives'; 'both joined and separate'), act-grounded at p.21, compensatory to division at p.22. Calleja-side 'exegetically inadmissible' caveat ANSWERED from the Burke side: textually grounded in Burke though Burke absent from Calleja — homology FUNCTIONAL not lexical (Burke tension T2).

homology_alignments: Calleja R1 assimilation (env INTO consciousness) <-> Burke 'A is substantially one with' the other (p.21)
Calleja R2 embodiment (player INTO env via avatar = single systemically-upheld locus) <-> Burke 'yet remains an individual locus of motives ... both joined and separate' (p.21)
Calleja R3 simultaneity <-> Burke both-joined-AND-separate (one in act yet two in being, p.21)
Calleja R4/R5 cornerstone+blending <-> Burke 'acting-together makes men consubstantial' (co-action, p.21)
Calleja incorporation-at-its-fullest <-> Burke ultimate identification (RM-07 p.333)
five_divergences: 1 medium of union: symbolic-substance vs phenomenological-absorption
2 ontological status: real-or-persuaded vs sustained-but-fleeting experiential state
3 grounding theory: substance-metaphysics vs experientialist embodied cognition (NOT Merleau-Ponty/Heidegger)
5 scope: society-wide + self-address + by-default vs bounded-to-ergodic-media
